item.title: Iran escalates in Hormuz, claims strike on Omani island it says 'enemy' uses for US military ops
item.description: Iran claims its Revolutionary Guard struck navigation equipment on Oman's Didamar Island in the Strait of Hormuz, but Omani officials dispute damage.
item.content:encoded:
Iran claims it struck a small Omani island in the Strait of Hormuz, targeting oil tanker navigation infrastructure as CENTCOM maintains its blockade of Iranian ports and protects commercial shipping from Iranian attacks along the southern route.

Three sources also confirmed to Reuters on Wednesday that navigation systems and communications equipment on Didamar Island, also known as Little Quoin Island, had been attacked, raising concerns about the vulnerability of maritime infrastructure used to maintain oil shipments through the Gulf.

Iran's semiofficial Fars News Agency reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy targeted the island, alleging the systems were being used to help vessels transit the strait without Tehran's authorization.

WHITE HOUSE SILENT ON IRAN-OMAN HORMUZ PLAN TEHRAN SAYS WOULD BAN US WARSHIPS

Iranian state television also claimed that personnel and equipment on the island "were helping the flow of oil smuggling by the enemy," with the IRGC maintaining it had carried out the strikes, Reuters reported.

Video published by Reuters showed smoke rising near the rocky outcrop.

The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) meanwhile, said it identified the attack as occurring Nov. 8, before Iranian state media claimed responsibility on Nov. 10.

ISW also questioned the extent of the reported damage, noting that commercial vessels continued using the southern route following the attack.

"The extent of the damage to these systems and the systems struck remains unclear at the time of this writing," ISW said in its assessment.

Satellite imagery from the European Union's Copernicus Sentinel-2 program, cited by Reuters and dated Nov. 8, also showed apparent scorch marks near radar and radio equipment on the island.

TRADE VESSEL STRUCK BY PROJECTILE IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ AMID US-IRAN TALKS

The strike comes as U.S forces carry out missions to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

The U.S. Navy imposed its blockade of Iranian ports in April after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in February amid escalating tensions. The U.S. lifted the blockade in June following a temporary ceasefire agreement, but then reinstated it in July.

Commercial and allied shipping through the waterway is advised to use a southern route through Omani territorial waters, located outside of Tehran’s direct military control and overseen by CENTCOM.

The latest incident on Didamar Island comes as Gulf oil exporters work to restore shipments disrupted by the conflict.

TRUMP MEETS KEY IRAN WAR MEDIATOR AS UAE REVEALS MAJOR OIL EXPORT SURGE DESPITE CONFLICT

According to Reuters, regional oil exports recovered to more than 80% of prewar levels in September and October, aided by CENTCOM and increased Saudi exports through the Red Sea.

Shipping companies have also relied on offshore tanker-to-tanker transfers near Oman and the United Arab Emirates to maintain flows.

Didamar, meanwhile, belongs to Oman, making the reported attack particularly sensitive as Tehran seeks to disrupt maritime operations in the region. It is a small, uninhabited rocky island roughly 10 nautical miles north of the tip of Oman's Musandam Peninsula, near one of the principal commercial shipping routes through the strait.

The island has long served as a navigational landmark for vessels traveling along the waterway, including through a lighthouse established in 1914.

Its maritime infrastructure reportedly includes a radar system mounted on a roughly 25-meter tower and radio communications equipment used to assist vessels navigating the narrow passage.

The island has also been associated with the Hormuz Control Centre, which coordinates maritime traffic in the area.

OIL SQUEEZE TIGHTENS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS CRIPPLE HORMUZ ESCAPE ROUTES

Arabian Maritime and Navigation Aids Services (AMMAS) has been identified as a provider of navigational support infrastructure in the region, including maritime lights, buoys and other equipment.

The reported Didamar attack also follows U.S. military operations against Iranian targets elsewhere in the waterway.

U.S. forces struck targets on Iran's Qeshm Island on Nov. 2, with officials describing the strikes as "defensive" actions targeting Iranian surface-to-air missile threats.

Qeshm Island, located near the Strait of Hormuz, is home to Iranian naval facilities and military infrastructure associated with the Revolutionary Guard.

President Donald Trump has also acknowledged Nov. 6. that American forces continue to conduct limited strikes against Iranian targets.

Asked by a reporter about the strikes near Qeshm Island, he said: "I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device, and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five."

item.title: Mississippi State’s Kamario Taylor finalizing a reported $7.5 million deal, in expensive college football move
item.description: Kamario Taylor's reported $7.5 million deal to stay at Mississippi State could reach $9 million with bonuses, matching mid first-round draft money.
item.content:encoded:
How much will it take for college football programs to re-sign their top quarterbacks heading into the 2027 season? Just ask Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor.

We have entered new territory when it comes to paying college athletes, especially in this era of NIL and revenue-sharing that has transcended the sports world.

College quarterbacks are making upwards of $6 to $7 million this season to lead their respective teams on the field, with that number only growing over the next few years as the price continues to trend upwards.

If you want an example of how much college sports have turned into a professional model, Mississippi State is finalizing a new deal with star quarterback Kamario Taylor that On3 reported will pay him $7.5 million next season for his services, and that number could jump to around $9 million if he collects incentive bonuses.

Wanting to stay Starkville has always been a priority for Taylor, who spent a lot of time before even enrolling at Mississippi State cheering on the Bulldogs. But, the ongoing talking-points around the sport of college football have centered around why Kamario should go chase a bigger paycheck somewhere else following the 2026 season.

BYU HAS THRIVED IN AN NIL ERA THAT MANY EXPECTED THEM TO FALTER IN, NFL LEGEND STEVE YOUNG SAYS

Whether it was numerous media pundits floating the idea that he would be happier somewhere else other than Starkville, the Bulldogs quarterback made it known to the coaching staff that he did not want to play elsewhere next season, and he wasn’t chasing the 'bag'.

But, that didn’t mean Mississippi State donors weren’t going to make sure their talented quarterback wasn’t taken care of from a financial standpoint, and they weren’t going to take the risk of some other team making him think twice about his decision.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT

This is the growing trend in college athletics. Conference commissioners and school officials can lobby all they want about reigning in the sport, but money will continue to talk.

And, if you think some schools are going to sit by and watch others swoop in to steal their talented players, you don't understand the pull that a place like Mississippi State can put together to entice athletes to stay.

After suffering a turf-toe injury earlier in the season, Kamario Taylor decided that surgery was the best option for him to be at 100% when the Bulldogs started their off-season training. So, now that his deal to return to Starkville in 2027 is complete, head coach Jeff Lebby can start building around its star quarterback through the transfer portal for next season.

It is a massive deal for the Mississippi State athletic department to have the former Heisman Trophy contender returning for another season, especially from a marketing standpoint.

Essentially, the money that the school and donors will pay Taylor for his services will be worth the contract he signs to stay in Starkville.

And yes, he's making mid-first-round draft pick money for the next calendar year.

If you thought this type of salary was a lot in college athletics, wait till you see what some of the other top college football players will garner as we get closer to the end of the regular season and the transfer portal prepares to open.

Money well spent by the Bulldogs, in this 'professional' world of college athletics.

item.title: State Department official blasts 'moronic' Washington Post report on Marco Rubio's required military flights
item.description: The State Department called a Washington Post report on Secretary of State Marco Rubio's military aircraft use "moronic," noting he is required to fly on government planes.
item.content:encoded:
A State Department official blasted The Washington Post on Wednesday, accusing the paper of publishing a "moronic" report that criticized Secretary of State Marco Rubio for using a military aircraft when he is required to do so. 

The Post published the story, "Flying by pricey military jet, Rubio rarely misses a Florida football game," which noted that the Secretary of State "is required to travel by government plane" when visiting his alma mater, where his son currently plays on the team.

The piece characterized Rubio’s trips as a "cost to taxpayers," and reported that his personal flights "have cost the government more than $1.2 million."

RUBIO HEADS TO ROME WITH TRUMP’S IRAN CLASH LOOMING OVER POPE, MELONI TALKS

"Like the defense secretary and the directors of the FBI and CIA, Rubio is barred from flying commercially for security reasons and is required, when traveling for personal reasons, to reimburse the government the equivalent of an economy-fare ticket," wrote Post reporters Noah White and Rick Maese.

"Officials’ reimbursements are rarely made public, but the amounts required cover only a fraction of the true cost, occasionally leading to scrutiny and controversy for Republican and Democratic appointees alike," they added. 

Rubio defended the trips, telling the paper, "I have and will continue to try and make it to as many events that are important to me personally and to my family as possible."

RUBIO TO VISIT ITALY, VATICAN AMID TROOP DRAWDOWN CALL, TENSION WITH TRUMP, POPE LEO: REPORTS

A government ethics expert told the Post that "Rubio’s travel complies with federal rules," but "raises a question about stewardship of public money." The Post also noted that former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg faced an audit over personal travel during the Biden administration, while pointing out that the "transportation secretary is not among the Cabinet members required to travel on military aircraft."

Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs Dylan Johnson criticized the report on X, saying the "Post’s own story quotes watchdogs saying this isn’t a story and there’s nothing here."

Johnson noted that the Secretary of State is required to use military aircraft, Rubio is "entirely unapologetic and will continue to attend as many of his family’s events as his jobs allow," he reimburses the government for personal travel and that the Buttigieg comparison is "moronic" because the former transportation secretary's position did not require him to use military aircraft.

The State Department did not immediately respond when asked for additional comment.

The report also drew criticism on social media.

"The Washington Post is trying to make a scandal out of Secretary Rubio traveling to attend his son's football games," former White House press advisor Pat Adams wrote. "They admit he's required to travel by government plane and that his trips all comply with federal rules, but they published the story anyway to suggest impropriety." 

"Most parents do whatever they can to see their children compete, but the Washington Post tries to paint that as bad judgment. Completely absurd article," he added.

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, now a Fox News contributor, wrote on X, "Washington Post confirms Secretary Rubio is a great dad."

The Post's report also noted that "senior officials have long used government planes for occasional personal travel," adding that the practice became a requirement in 1993.

The Washington Post did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Josh Downs has hilarious reaction after being traded from reeling Colts to contending Chiefs
item.description: Josh Downs had a hilarious reaction on social media after the Indianapolis Colts traded him to the Kansas City Chiefs ahead of the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
You think Josh Downs was happy to get out of Indianapolis?

The 25-year-old requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts after they traded Pro Bowl offensive lineman Quenton Nelson and All-Pro DeForest Buckner in October, and his wish was granted on Tuesday. The Colts traded Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks.

Downs took to social media to express his jubilation from being traded from the reeling Colts to the contending Chiefs. He posted a GIF of an exultant Vince Carter from his retirement ceremony, indicating his excitement about the trade. In a separate post, Downs thanked the Colts.

"I am beyond grateful and blessed for my time in Indy. Nothing but love For the Shoe," Downs wrote on X.

Downs became the fourth player the Colts traded before Tuesday’s trade deadline, joining Nelson, Buckner and wide receiver Keenan Allen.

With the Chiefs, Downs will provide an immediate boost to a unit that has struggled to produce this season. Rashee Rice leads Chiefs wide receivers with just 292 receiving yards this season.

Downs has spent his entire four-year NFL career with the Colts after Indianapolis selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of North Carolina.

item.title: Death reported in E coli outbreak linked to California pumpkin patch as more cases emerge
item.description: An E. coli outbreak linked to California’s Brookshire Farms has left one person dead, five confirmed infections and 10 suspected cases.
item.content:encoded:
One person has died in an E. coli outbreak linked to a California pumpkin farm, San Luis Obispo County health officials confirmed Tuesday. Officials have not released the person’s age or identity.

The death follows confirmation of five cases of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection, potentially originating from Brookshire Farms in San Luis Obispo, according to an advisory issued by the County of San Luis Obispo Public Health Department.

"We can confirm that one individual associated with the E. coli outbreak has died. We are sharing this information with the permission of the individual’s family," Tom Cuddy, public information officer for the department, said in a statement to The Tribune of San Luis Obispo on Nov. 10.

E. COLI OUTBREAK LANDS 3 IN HOSPITAL; HEALTH OFFICIALS INVESTIGATE LINK TO PUMPKIN PATCH

"This is truly a heartbreaking development, and our thoughts are with the family and everyone affected by this outbreak. The entire team at Public Health extends our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones during this difficult time."

In a Nov. 6 statement, the health department said an additional 10 individuals who visited the farm between Oct. 16 and Oct. 26 and developed symptoms have been deemed "suspect cases." 

Tests of water, food and other samples from the farm found some bacteria, including other E. coli strains, but did not detect the strain responsible for the outbreak, officials said.

People who became ill shared possible exposures to corn cups, pumpkins, hay and water not intended for drinking, but officials could not pinpoint the source.

FDA WIDENS CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK INVESTIGATION TO SIX MORE STATES AS CONFIRMED CASES TOP 6,000

No farm animals or petting zoos, which are known to be common sources of this type of infection, were accessible to visitors or operating at the farm.

Investigators faced several limitations, including numerous possible sources, items no longer available for testing and delays between exposure and sampling. No further environmental testing is planned, according to the report.

"Based on the findings of our investigation, we believe the risk of additional exposure associated with this incident has passed, and there is no longer an ongoing public health threat," said County Health Officer Dr. Christy Mulkerin.

"Our hearts go out to the families affected by this outbreak. We thank all those who have helped protect our community in response to this outbreak, and we encourage community members to continue practicing good handwashing and food safety to protect themselves and their families."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Typical symptoms of E. coli include cramping, severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea and signs of dehydration, which usually begin within three to 10 days of exposure.

Young children under 10 are typically at the highest risk for complications, which can include hemolytic uremic syndrome, a serious condition that damages blood cells and can lead to kidney failure, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Dr. Tyler Evans, an infectious disease physician and founder of Wellness Equity Alliance in California, warned that diarrhea can lead to dehydration and fatigue.

"The diarrhea is really the key component here, and the stomach cramps," he told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Evans said younger children and older adults can be particularly vulnerable, emphasizing the need to closely watch children younger than 5.

Speaking generally about potential exposure routes in pumpkin patches, Evans said E. coli can spread when bacteria from feces reach someone’s mouth.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

He pointed to potentially contaminated food or water, animal contact and person-to-person transmission as possible transmission routes.

Evans also noted that not all E. coli bacteria cause illness. The confirmed cases in this investigation involve Shiga toxin-producing E. coli.

The health department shared the following safe practices to protect against these types of infections.

Fox News Digital reached out to the county health department for comment. Brookshire Farms previously told Fox News Digital it was reserving comment pending test results.

item.title: Lindsey Vonn gives health update as she undergoes ninth surgery following brutal Olympic crash
item.description: Lindsey Vonn revealed she's heading into her ninth surgery to remove plates and screws before finally getting a new ACL after her Olympic crash.
item.content:encoded:
It's been nearly ten months since Lindsey Vonn sustained brutal injuries in a crash at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, and the skiing star revealed that her recovery is still very much ongoing.

The 42-year-old five-time Olympian hopped on social media to inform her followers that she had gone in for surgery.

For the ninth time.

LINDSEY VONN ALL SMILES AS SHE'S ABLE TO RETURN TO DUMPING OUT ACTUAL WORKOUT CONTENT AGAIN

"This will be my ninth surgery," Vonn said in the video. 'I'm doing this beforehand because I'm actually getting pretty nervous about it. On the day of, I'm going to be focused and rested and trying to get through it."

Vonn explained that the reason for this surgery was to remove hardware that had been installed during previous procedures.

"Basically, what we're doing is removing all of the plates and screws and just basically removing all the hardware to make room for the new ACL because I don't have an ACL still because of all the plates; just couldn't put it in," she explained.

Back in February, she was competing on a torn ACL in her left leg that she injured just before the start of the games. She tried to compete in the Olympics, but crashed in the women's downhill event and severely injured the same leg.

LINDSEY VONN KEEPS THE BIRTHDAY CELEBRATION GOING, SLIPPING INTO A BODYSUIT FOR CLOTHING LINE'S NEW COLLECTION

However, once she has that fresh ACL, she still has a long road ahead of her.

"So I've been waiting all these nine months so my bones could heal and we could fix the ACL, and my bones healed, which is great news," she said. "But obviously now I have the ACL, and that means another six-to-nine months."

Fortunately, Vonn posted on her Instagram story that the surgery went well.

She also showed off a big with the hardware that used to be in her left leg captioned, "Got all this s--t out of my leg."

item.title: Stephen A Smith says white players are not good enough to win NBA championships
item.description: Stephen A. Smith claims the Los Angeles Lakers can't win a championship because Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler are white.
item.content:encoded:
Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers are statistically the best overall trio in the NBA this season. Yet ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith says the trio isn't good enough to win a championship.

He doesn't cite their play as the reason, but rather their skin color.

"I do not think [the Lakers] are getting past the second round. I’d be shocked if they did. I am on the record being controversially because I’ve never seen an NBA team with its top players being White deliver a championship. It’s never happened. And I’m here to tell you I don’t think it’s going to happen this year.

"You can bring up whoever the hell you want," Smith said. "There has never been, in my lifetime, an NBA team led with its top three players being White that delivered you a championship when an abundance of brothers [are] playing basketball. That hasn’t happened. And I’m here to tell you it ain’t gonna happen. I can’t see it coming."

Oh.

Smith first made this argument in July, though he presented it differently. Then, he claimed he had "never seen" a team with three White stars win a championship. He clarified that he never said it "couldn't" happen.

This time, he repeatedly dismissed the possibility of a team winning a championship led by "three White dudes."

BOBBY BURACK: RYAN CLARK CLAIMS ESPN INTERVIEWED SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ABOUT TRANS ATHLETES TO IMPRESS OUTKICK

Smith provides no basketball explanation for why three White players can't lead a team to a title. That's likely because there isn't one. His premise doesn't withstand even mild scrutiny.

The simplest explanation for why an all-White Big 3 has yet to win a championship is the racial breakdown of the NBA. White players make up roughly 17% of the league, compared with about 75% for Black players. Fewer white players means fewer White stars, making it less likely that three will play on the same team.

It's really that simple.

BOBBY BURACK: DIANNA RUSSINI WANTS SYMPATHY WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY IN MIKE VRABEL SCANDAL

It's the same reason an NFL team has never won a Super Bowl with a Black quarterback, Black head coach and Black general manager.

Imagine using that data point to argue a team must have at least a White coach or general manager to win a Super Bowl. Smith would be among the first commentators to denounce you as a racist if you made that argument.

Racial double standards are real. They are obvious.

Therefore, Smith will not face any considerable backlash for his comments about the Lakers. Society has decided that Black people are permitted to make racist, belittling comments about White people – just not the other way around.

It's why former NBA player Charlie Villanueva can casually claim Doncic cannot be the best player in a "Black league." It's why WNBA players could just as casually claim Caitlin Clark needed to pay her respects to the Black women before her.

There is a particularly notable use of possessive language when certain Black basketball players discuss their White counterparts. They often use the term "ours" when discussing the NBA and WNBA. The implication is that White players are allowed to participate but ought to know their place.

It's no different from activist and social media influencer Dr. Umar Johnson's recent dismissal of Eminem's place in hip-hop history. In Johnson's view, hip-hop also belongs to Black people.

"No non-African can ever be the best of anything African. It's an insult to the ancestors. It's an insult to the race, and it's an insult to every Black person," Johnson said. "Eminem has all the privileges of a White male and all the privileges of being in the hip-hop community, so we got to be careful about letting non-Africans into our community."

Wait, who has privilege again? The people accused of it, or the people exhibiting it with racially charged rhetoric toward the opposite race?

Combating supposed racism with coordinated racism is not the answer. Racism will never go away if certain people feel emboldened to spread it.

Finally, there is an amusing flaw in Smith's assessment of the Lakers' championship aspirations. Despite the league-leading production from Doncic, Reaves, and Kessler, the Lakers have just the 10th-best championship odds.

The concern is the supporting cast around them. That cast is entirely Black.

If Stephen A. insists on blaming the Lakers' championship limitations on the race of certain players, he's blaming the wrong group.

It's not the "White dudes" holding them back.

item.title: Multiple people pulled from rubble after NYC building collapse, search underway for others feared trapped
item.description: Emergency crews are on the scene after a building collapsed in Brooklyn. Search-and-rescue operations are underway, and the surrounding area has been evacuated.
item.content:encoded:
The New York City Fire Department (FDNY) is responding after a three-story building collapsed Wednesday in New York City, trapping people inside.

Two people were removed from the Brooklyn structure in the borough's Flatbush neighborhood and were being evaluated, the FDNY told Fox News Digital. 

In total, five people were taken to Kings County Hospital in unknown condition, according to the New York City Police Department (NYPD).

item.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: JonBenét Ramsey's father challenges DA after report says family shouldn't have been cleared

item.title: Ring of Honor champ Deonna Purrazzo bringing wrestling to NJ town to raise awareness about major issue
item.description: Deonna Purrazzo teams with Steve Maclin at Jefferson Township High School to spotlight New Jersey's S-2 funding formula crisis hitting Highlands schools.
item.content:encoded:
Ring of Honor women’s pure champion Deonna Purrazzo is set to return to her hometown in New Jersey to help raise money for her alma mater high school and raise awareness about the lack of funding for the schools in that area of the state.

Purrazzo’s JTown SmackDown will take place at Jefferson Township High School in Oak Ridge on Friday night. The event means more than just teaming up with her husband, fellow pro wrestling star Steve Maclin. She is looking to put the spotlight on a serious issue that is near to her heart.

"I've worked with the athletic director, Bill Koch, for the past few months, since earlier this year, really, when we were reconnected over the Highlands Impact Aid Now rally at Jefferson, where we're trying to draw attention to the fact that the funding formula for schools in New Jersey, the S-2 funding formula is not fair," Purrazzo told OutKick Dropkick. "It's not equitable to the students of the Highlands and the Pinelands.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

"And so that kind of was the precipice to JTown SmackDown. We were raising money for the athletic department and for the JTEF, the Jefferson Township Educational Fund, which is all going to the students."

New Jersey’s S-2 funding formula was enacted as part of a revision to the 2008 School Funding Reform Act, which was meant to take aim at funding inadequacies across the state. But Purrazzo and other local officials have said it’s created a bigger issue for the township.

Part of the issue, Purrazzo has said, is the Highlands Act. The piece of legislation protects hundreds of thousands acres of land in the Highlands, which is the main source of drinking water for millions of residents in New Jersey. The act comes with development restrictions, which critics have said hampers growth in places like Jefferson Township.

"The S-2 funding formula and how it affects the Highlands is multifaceted. Fifteen or so years ago, there was a piece of legislation put in place in the Highlands that restricted the growth of the land in the tax base. And so, 88% of Jefferson Township is under this protection where new businesses can't come in, affordable housing can't be built, you can't rent out houses or build on your property because all of the land is protected. They provide millions and millions of gallons of water to all across New Jersey every single day. While environmental protection is important, it's limiting the growth of our students.

"What's happened because of that is taxes have risen in town. We've lost the funding formula because people are moving out of town. Enrollment is how they equate funding for the schools. And so because our enrollments down, the funding goes down ... It's not been fair. Meanwhile, cities like Newark are able to build new buildings and hire new teachers and all these things that Jefferson Township and the surrounding towns are just not able to do. So, the awareness is coming from, we have to refigure out how this formula works, especially in these towns where the tax base isn't allowed to grow, and how do we make it equitable for these towns who literally can't up their enrollment."

The New Jersey Education Association said last month it was taking on the task of rewriting the funding formula with the hope that it would be implemented during the 2027-28 school year.

Jefferson Township Superintendent Jeanne Howe warned in March that the district could have to make cuts and increase classroom sizes if money doesn’t start to flow in, according to the Morristown Daily Record.

In recent years, New Jersey lawmakers have worked together to provide millions of dollars to districts that saw reductions in funding because of the S-2 formula.

Purrazzo hopes that a return to her high school would put the issue in a larger spotlight. She recalled speaking at one of the rallies earlier this year, which took place at the high school as well.

"I don't know how I'm gonna react because when I was there in March for the Highlands Impact Aid rally, I spoke and I gave like a 7 or 8 minute speech about how growing up in this town really shaped my character for the rest of my life and allowed me to become a six-time world champion and travel the world as a professional wrestler, but they played my entrance music when I walked up to the podium and I started crying, which I didn't expect, right?

" I was just overwhelmed with, there were so many familiar faces in the crowd, and obviously, it's for such a great cause. I'm getting a master's degree in political science, but I've never really stepped on a stage and spoken about policies and legislation, things that I was doing that day. So it was definitely a step out of my comfort zone, but really rewarding to be able to start there and now have worked through producing a wrestling show. I don't know exactly how I'm gonna feel. There might be a few tears, but it'll all be worth it."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Purrazzo and Maclin will take on VSK and Emily Jaye, Goldy will go up against Griffin McCoy Tiara James will square off against Tina San Antonio and Oxx Adams will face off against Marcus Mathers.

Jaye is a highly talented young women’s wrestler who is among the next crop of talent that pro wrestling fans should pay attention to. She made her All Elite Wrestling debut earlier this year and has performed at several promotions from Gamechanger Wrestling to Boca Raton Championship Wrestling.

Purrazzo said her advice to someone like Jaye is the same for any up-and-coming female star.

"I say to her exactly what I say to all the women's wrestlers who are coming up right now: Don't quit on yourself," she told OutKick Dropkick. "There's going to be so many people who, for me, didn't know what ‘The Virtuosa’ meant, didn't see the vision in it, didn't understand that it's not this like overt in your face character. It is very nuanced, but it is very me, and I believed in it and I knew that if someone would give me the investment and the opportunity to educate the audience in terms of what that meant for me, it would click. And so, my biggest advice to Emily and all of the women coming up right now is, if you have a vision for yourself and you believe in it 100%, don't let anyone's opinions deter you. Don't quit on yourself."

JTown Smackdown will begin at 7 p.m. ET.

item.title: NYC parents and locals protest homeless men's shelter being built a short walk from middle school
item.description: Canarsie residents erupted in protest Monday night over a 200-bed homeless men's shelter planning to be built one block from a Brooklyn middle school.
item.content:encoded:
Parents across Brooklyn's Canarsie neighborhood are demanding answers from New York City officials and Mayor Zohran Mamdani over plans to build a 200-bed men's homeless shelter just one block from a local middle school.

Parents, teachers and other residents protested Monday night against plans for a 200-bed men's homeless shelter on East 108th Street that is expected to open in 2028, one block from the Science and Medicine Middle School 366 on East 107th Street.

Among the protesters was New York City Council member Mercedes Narcisse, who represents the 46th District and criticized the city's Department of Social Services (DSS) in comments reported by News 12 Brooklyn.

SEE IT: MASSIVE NYC HOMELESS ENCAMPMENT FUELS BACKLASH AGAINST MAMDANI

"You want to put it next to a school — a middle school for God's sake! These are our children! Shame!" Narcisse said.

Narcisse said DSS informed her about the proposed shelter last week but had not sought her input, even though she represents the neighborhood.

According to News 12 Brooklyn, the upcoming shelter is part of a broader citywide plan to open 12 new shelters, including three in Brooklyn.

PARENTS IN BRONX NEIGHBORHOOD PLEAD FOR NYPD GUARD AS MAMDANI CUTS COPS, HALTS HIRES: 'HORRIBLE SITUATION'

Narcisse has requested a meeting with the DSS commissioner for Thursday to discuss residents' concerns. However, many protesters are calling for New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to attend.

"I asked for the commissioner, but now, my community says the mayor," Narcisse said.

DSS confirmed plans to construct more shelters across the city and emphasized community engagement as part of the process.

"Notifying elected officials and community boards is a part of the public process around siting new shelters. Notification is the beginning of a process that includes opportunity for community engagement," DSS told Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Science and Medicine Middle School 366, Narcisse's office and Mamdani's office for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

FURIOUS RESIDENTS CONFRONT HOMELESS HOUSING LEADERS AS POPULAR BEACH COMMUNITY HITS BREAKING POINT

The protest follows other demonstrations across New York City over plans to open men's homeless shelters, with residents criticizing what they say is a lack of community input.

In July, the New York Post reported that the city moved 110 single homeless men into a former family shelter in Brooklyn. According to the report, the city's Department of Homeless Services did not conduct criminal background checks on the men before the relocation.

item.title: Fiery chaos erupts across Spain as protesters clash with police during massive nationwide strike
item.description: Spain's first general strike in 14 years turned violent in Barcelona as protesters set fires and launched fireworks at riot police on Paseo de Gracia.
item.content:encoded:
Unruly protesters set fires, smashed storefronts and launched fireworks at riot police across parts of Spain on Wednesday as a massive nationwide strike over soaring housing costs disrupted transportation and businesses.

Violent scenes unfolded in Barcelona, where some demonstrators vandalized stores along the city's popular Paseo de Gracia shopping boulevard, set small bonfires and launched fireworks at officers arriving in riot gear and armored vehicles, according to The Associated Press.

The violence erupted after a largely peaceful march as Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years, with workers demanding relief from skyrocketing rents and the rising cost of living.

TRAVELERS MAY FACE MAJOR DISRUPTIONS AS STRIKES THREATEN AIRPORTS AND POPULAR ATTRACTIONS

Housing activists claimed 400,000 people marched through Barcelona, while city officials estimated attendance at 55,000. Government officials reported another 120,000 demonstrators gathered in Madrid despite heavy rain, the AP reported.

The nationwide walkout disrupted public transportation, forced some businesses to close and blocked major roads. Police made arrests across the country, while officers used pepper spray against demonstrators in Madrid, according to the AP.

ANGRY LOCALS BLOCK FAMOUS BEACH AS MASS TOURISM PROTESTS ESCALATE AT VACATION HOT SPOT

The unrest comes amid growing frustration over Spain's housing crisis, fueled in part by the eviction of an 87-year-old Madrid woman who had lived in her apartment for seven decades before reportedly facing a tripling of her rent. She died weeks later, according to the BBC.

The housing crisis has become a major political flashpoint ahead of Spain's Nov. 29 parliamentary elections, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez reportedly encouraging workers to exercise their right to strike.

SPANISH OPPOSITION LEADER CALLS PRIME MINISTER A ‘TRAITOR’ OVER CEUTA MIGRANT CRISIS

But the demonstrations have also sparked a political clash, with conservative opposition leaders accusing Sánchez's government of exploiting the unrest for electoral gain, according to the BBC.

Meanwhile, Spain's largest labor unions declared the ongoing strike a success despite business groups disputing claims of widespread participation.

item.title: Eli Drinkwitz calls out college football’s identity crisis as CFP expansion buries tradition
item.description: Eli Drinkwitz questions why conferences exist without championship games, saying college football has devalued what once made the sport special.
item.content:encoded:
You can add Missouri's Eli Drinkwitz to the growing list of coaches around college football that are questioning the future of the sport, and how we arrived at this point.

An ever-changing landscape that has seen college athletics shift towards a more pay-for-play system as if that wasn’t the case before NIL arrived on the scene has led to a number of changes within the sport of football.

CFP REACTION: ALABAMA FEELS THE LOVE, INDIANA GETS THE SHAFT AND BIG 12 GETS RELIEF AS COMMITTEE CONFUSES US

Whether that be the amount of players who are now chasing playing time and the biggest paycheck through the transfer portal or the expansion of a college football playoff that is only three years into its current form of 12 teams, it's clear that conferences across the country are doing their best to hold on for dear life during these times of economic questions.

Sure, nobody is crying for these head coaches that are bringing home multi-million-dollar checks on a yearly basis, with buyouts that have become even more outrageous over the years.

But, no matter what you think of the economics encompassing a head coach, it doesn’t mean they are wrong when voicing their opinions on the current state of college athletics.

One of those current conversations incapsulating the sport of football centers around the elimination of the conference championship games, thanks to the CFP expanding to 24 teams.

"Why are we associated with conferences anymore if we’re not playing for a conference championship?" Drinkwitz asked. "I mean, if the point now is just to be playing into the seat of 24, are we just doing it for scheduling affiliation? And if we’re just doing it for scheduling affiliation, are we, is there a reason to be flying all the way across the country to play games from a national perspective?

"I think that’s where this conversation is going to end up leading to."

COLLEGE FOOTBALL SELLS ANOTHER PIECE OF ITS SOUL WITH CFP OFFICIALLY EXPANDING TO 24 TEAMS

He's not wrong, though there is much more to being in a conference than just a championship game, and I would say Drinkwitz would admit that.

But, this goes back to the inception of NIL, when it sent us down a path of no return. When players rightfully started being paid, the NCAA had no rules around how to navigate the new era, and neither did the conferences.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF EXPANSION IS NOTHING MORE THAN A DESPERATE FINANCIAL BAILOUT DISGUISED AS PROGRESS

That's just a byproduct though of the current situation that is causing athletic directors to lose sleep at night around financing each sport on their campus.

"The decisions we'e made in college football over the last six years, and we've made them to where we are at now. I think when you look back, we’ve devalued some of the things that made college football so special. Bowl games are no longer valuable," Drinkwitz noted. "Building a program and having a season to build for the next season, where your fans could be excited about these guys playing, ‘OK, man, next year this got a chance.’ There’s none of that because you don’t know who’s going to be back. Every team’s starting over each year.

"There’s no real regional rivalries anymore because there’s no more regional conferences outside of ours, which is the best conference in college football."

The short answer to that question is no, the CFP did not take the input of the college football fans into their decision to move forward with a 24-team postseason.

And, that's the problem.

Sure, fans are going to tune into these additional games that are played at regular season's end, but that doesn’t mean the product is worth watching. For the diehards, if you put a college football game on television, there will be viewers.

Look at the excitement that comes with Tuesday and Wednesday night MAC-tion that provides us with competition during the week.

"We've made a lot of decisions and we've asked a lot of people their opinions," Drinkwitz lamented. "But have we cared about the fans?

"I don't know the answer to that question. Do I think the conference championship games were a good thing? Yes, I do, I think they were great. Do I think they're no longer important? Yea, I agree with the assessment that there really is no reason to play them."

We have a lot of problems to deal with in college athletics, and the near future is going to tell is a lot about how leaders are going to handle it.

item.title: Trump's ex-lawyer Alina Habba loses massive contract days after president blasts 'outrageous' deal

Concord Partners, a Florida-based company founded by Isabela Herrera, daughter of Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini, terminated Habba Mildon’s contract after President Donald Trump urged the Herrera family to stop paying her, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday.

Concord Partners cited a "failure to perform duties" in a Nov. 4 termination letter obtained by The New York Times.

Herrera faced federal bribery charges tied to an alleged scheme involving Puerto Rico’s governor and struck a plea deal accepting a misdemeanor campaign finance violation in August 2025.

The firing came just days after Trump publicly blasted Habba Mildon’s $50 million arrangement as excessive and said he did not want her to receive the money.

Habba Mildon signed the agreement with Concord Partners in October 2025 while serving as acting U.S. attorney for New Jersey. She began working for the company on Jan. 1, 2026, after becoming a senior advisor to Attorney General Pam Bondi, according to the outlet.

item.title: Longtime GOP leader faces uncertain future after Jim Jordan wins House leadership fight
item.description: Steve Scalise declined to commit to serving a full term in the 120th Congress after losing the House Republican minority leader race to Jim Jordan.
item.content:encoded:
House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., the No. 2 Republican in the House of Representatives and the most tenured figure among the chamber's party leadership, declined to say whether he would commit to serving the full term in the upcoming 120th Congress.

"There’s no decision on what’s next," Scalise said on Wednesday.

"I’ve got to get through these next few weeks, and then we have a lot of decisions to make about what's life going to look like in the minority. But I sure still have a great passion for this country."

JIM JORDAN THROWS HAT IN RING FOR HOUSE MINORITY LEADER AS GOP PICKS UP PIECES AFTER BLUE WAVE

Scalise’s answer follows a loss to Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, in a bid to become the party’s new minority leader. His defeat now forces Scalise to decide whether he intends to retire or remain on Capitol Hill as a rank-and-file member of the minority as Democrats retake control of the House in January.

For now, Scalise stressed that he remains focused on securing GOP priorities before the new year.

"There’s a lot more for us to do. We have a few weeks left in the lame duck [session] and, frankly, a few big, big issues ahead. I want to see us do as much as we possibly can while we still have this majority," Scalise said.

"I’ve got a lot more gas in the tank. Obviously, all of us know there’s some real change coming in January. We still have work to do right now."

Jordan beat out Scalise in a 106-73 vote in Tuesday’s GOP elections.

Scalise, who was elected in 2008 and first joined Republican leadership in 2014, proved a steady figure and mouthpiece for conservative principles even as the party shifted dramatically around him.

Scalise originally served as House whip alongside Speaker John Boehner, R-Ohio.

JORDAN EMERGES AS POTENTIAL NEXT GOP LEADER IF DEMS SEIZE HOUSE

Although Boehner would eventually step down after the right flank of the party accused him of failing to secure GOP priorities, Scalise remained a constant, continuing to serve as whip under his successor, Speaker Paul Ryan, R-Wis. Around the same time, Donald Trump, then just a candidate for president, began gaining momentum in the GOP primary.

As the party’s core began to gravitate toward Trump, Scalise’s time in Congress and personal well-being were challenged when he was shot at a congressional baseball practice in 2017.

Although the incident left him with health complications, the attack elevated Scalise’s national profile.

"Just left hospital. Rep. Steve Scalise, one of the truly great people, is in very tough shape — but he is a real fighter. Pray for Steve!" Trump said in a post to social media at the time.

In 2023, Scalise would climb to the No. 2 job, becoming majority leader after Republicans recaptured the House of Representatives under Speaker Kevin McCarthy, R-Calif.

And when McCarthy himself was removed from the post for failing to deliver Republican demands to cut spending, Scalise launched an unsuccessful bid for speaker.

Instead, Scalise remained majority leader as Republicans rallied around Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La.

Asked if he would have done anything differently in his most recent bid to lead the House GOP, Scalise said he had no regrets.

"Nothing that could have been done differently in the leadership race," Scalise said.

MIKE JOHNSON'S NO 2 LAUNCHES GOP TAKEOVER BID AS HOUSE FALLS TO DEMOCRATS

"There’s clearly a lot of weight lifted now. I mean, these leadership jobs take a lot of time, a lot of focus. I love doing the work… it takes you away from your family, from other things that you enjoy doing back home. I’ll have a little more free time there," he added.

Following the Nov. 3 midterm elections, Republicans have a little under seven weeks to press for legislative priorities with their majorities in the House and Senate.

The 120th Congress is set to begin on Jan. 3, 2027.

item.title: New weight-loss drug wipes out chronic knee pain in some patients, researchers say
item.description: Northwestern University-led trials found retatrutide helped two-thirds of obese knee osteoarthritis patients cut pain by half in late-stage studies.
item.content:encoded:
An experimental weight-loss drug significantly reduced chronic knee pain and improved mobility in people with obesity and knee osteoarthritis, according to two clinical trials led by researchers at Northwestern University.

The trials, which were funded by Eli Lilly and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, evaluated retatrutide, a once-weekly injectable medication developed by Eli Lilly and Co.

Retatrutide, which is not yet FDA-approved, mimics three hormones involved in appetite and metabolism — GLP-1, GIP and glucagon — and has produced substantial weight loss in clinical trials.

WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY FIGHT 7 SERIOUS HEALTH PROBLEMS BEFORE THE POUNDS EVEN COME OFF

The late-stage trials enrolled more than 1,000 adults who were overweight or obese, did not have diabetes, and experienced painful knee osteoarthritis.

After 68 weeks in one trial and 80 weeks in the other, participants receiving the highest dose of retatrutide lost about a quarter of their body weight on average. A pooled analysis found that roughly two-thirds of those treated with the drug achieved at least a 50% drop in knee pain, compared with 38% of those receiving a placebo.

Beyond pain relief and functional gains, participants experienced reductions in blood pressure, lower blood lipid levels and decreased systemic inflammation, according to the researchers.

Gastrointestinal problems were the most common side effects, and serious adverse events were more common among participants receiving retatrutide than among those receiving placebo.

KNEE TREATMENT WITHOUT SURGERY OFFERS LASTING PAIN RELIEF FOR 80% OF ARTHRITIS PATIENTS, STUDY FINDS

Dr. Thomas J. Schnitzer, a professor at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine and lead author of the study, said the findings offer therapeutic potential for specific groups of patients.

"For people who are obese, not diabetic, have radiographically confirmed knee osteoarthritis that has not progressed to bone on bone, and have consistent moderate knee pain, retatrutide treatment has the potential to result in a significant and meaningful reduction in their knee pain and improvement in their physical function while providing cardiometabolic benefit," Schnitzer told Fox News Digital.

While researchers anticipated benefits from the weight reduction, the "complete relief of knee pain" in one of every eight patients taking the drug was a surprise, Schnitzer said.

Painful knee osteoarthritis affects an estimated 15 million Americans, often turning routine activities such as standing, walking and climbing stairs into painful challenges.

YOUR FAVORITE SNACKS COULD BE QUIETLY WRECKING YOUR KNEES, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS

Conventional treatments include physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medications and steroid injections, which often offer only limited or temporary relief, according to the researchers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

While earlier research has found that losing 5% to 10% of body weight through diet and exercise can ease knee osteoarthritis symptoms, losing more than 10% through those measures alone can be difficult, particularly when knee pain limits exercise, Schnitzer said.

Despite the study's promising outcomes, Schnitzer stressed that there were some limitations.

"People with knee OA who were not overweight or obese were not studied, and individuals who were obese and had more advanced OA were also excluded, so we have no information on them," he said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The trials excluded patients who needed knee replacement surgery. Whether retatrutide slows osteoarthritis progression or reduces the need for future joint replacements remains unknown.

For individuals experiencing joint pain who may meet the study criteria, Schnitzer recommended discussing options with a healthcare provider.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"If someone fits the profile noted above, and they have been unsuccessful at losing weight, they should speak to their physician about the possibility of being treated with a medication that would help them lose weight, as that could also reduce their knee pain as well as provide cardiometabolic benefits," Schnitzer said.

At the same time, he emphasized that medication should not replace healthy daily habits.

"Before starting pharmacologic treatment for knee pain, people who are overweight should try diet and exercise and consider interventions such as physical therapy," Schnitzer advised.

"Also, even for people on weight-loss medications, exercise is an important part of any treatment plan to maintain as much muscle as possible."

item.title: DNA links 4 grizzly bears to deadly attack on mother and daughter in Canada, officials say
item.description: DNA evidence linked four grizzly bears to the deaths of Jennifer Balcarras and Selah Reed near Bella Coola, British Columbia, officials said.
item.content:encoded:
Four grizzly bears have been linked through DNA evidence to a deadly attack on a mother and daughter in British Columbia, prompting Canadian wildlife officers to kill all four animals, officials announced Tuesday.

The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said forensic testing conclusively linked an adult female grizzly and her three offspring to the deaths of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, near Bella Coola.

The bears were captured over the weekend and killed in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety, according to a Nov. 10 statement from the agency.

BODY OF MISSING HIKER DISCOVERED OFF TRAIL AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE RARE DEADLY BEAR ENCOUNTER

Investigators determined that the encounter likely involved predatory behavior, although officials did not elaborate on how the attack unfolded.

"This was a heartbreaking event for the families, the Nuxalk Nation and the Bella Coola community. We hope the efforts of everyone who responded, along with these findings, bring some measure of closure," said Insp. Jeff Tyre in a news briefing.

More than a dozen conservation officers participated in the response, helping recover the victims, collect evidence and locate the bears while working in difficult terrain and weather conditions.

GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL

Balcarras, an art therapist, and Reed went missing after taking a walk on the Snooka West Trail near their home.

Family members contacted the Royal Canadian Mounted Police after Balcarras missed a scheduled online meet-up. Investigators found her vehicle at the trailhead before recovering her body on Nov. 2 and Reed's body on Nov. 3.

The agency said DNA testing also confirmed the four bears were not involved in a separate 2025 grizzly bear attack on a school group near Bella Coola that injured 11 people, including students and teachers.

The investigation has concluded, although officials said further analysis will examine the response and circumstances surrounding the attack.

The conservation service said fatal grizzly bear attacks involving predatory behavior are rare and encouraged people traveling in bear country to leash pets, travel in groups and learn how to reduce the risk of wildlife encounters.

Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano contributed to this report.

item.title: Chiefs stick with Harrison Butker as kicker in Week 10 despite 7 missed field goals, Justin Tucker in waiting
item.description: Andy Reid confirmed Harrison Butker will start over Justin Tucker against the Atlanta Falcons despite Butker's league-leading seven missed field goals.
item.content:encoded:
Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid made his kicking decision for Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons.

Harrison Butker, who leads the NFL with seven missed field goals, will remain the team’s starting kicker on the road at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Justin Tucker, whom the Chiefs controversially signed to the practice squad, remains on the bench.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Butker’s status as the team’s starting kicker was in question after yet another miss during Week 9’s rout of the New York Jets. After missing on a field goal attempt from 51 yards that was blown dead, Butker couldn’t hit it on a second try.

A flurry of boos at Arrowhead Stadium rained on Butker, who even admitted, "I I’m booing myself sometimes."

ADAM VINATIERI WEIGHS IN ON CHIEFS KICKER BATTLE AFTER HELPING USAA IMPACT SERVICE MEMBERS IN GERMANY

Since the start of last season, Butker has missed a total 17 kicks – 12 field goals and five extra points – which is the most of any kicker in the league.

OutKick spoke with Pro Football Hall of Famer kicker Adam Vinatieri on Tuesday while he was in Germany supporting USAA ahead of the NFL’s Munich game between the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots. He believed the Chiefs would be running an open competition with Tucker, the 37-year-old veteran kicker, at practice.

Tucker was said to have an "off the charts" workout with the Chiefs, which led to his signing. However, Reid hasn’t pulled the plug on Butker just yet. He said he would "look at everything" this week, including the kicker position.

"You’d have to see how Justin’s doing as well, right?" Vinatieri said. "I mean, it’s always an open competition. The way I look at it, even if there’s not another kicker on your team, there’s always somebody out there. There’s 30 guys out there at any given time. It’s Harrison’s job to lose. He’s done a really, really nice job throughout his career. If he can right that ship and get it back, it’s his job, in my opinion. But like you said, as you get closer to playoffs, the margin of error is so much smaller."

Tucker’s signing comes after he served a 10-game NFL suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy following allegations of sexual misconduct by many massage therapists from eight different spas and wellness centers in the Baltimore Area during his time playing for the Ravens. The alleged misconduct occurred between 2012 and 2016.

While Tucker has vehemently denied the allegations, the NFL suspended him two months after being released by the Ravens in May 2025.

Tucker was reinstated in November, and previously tried out for the New Orleans Saints. But he’s been waiting his turn with the Chiefs now, as Butker looks to get a hold of his job back entering a crucial week for himself against the Falcons.

item.title: Stephen Miller's internal memo unleashes Trump agencies after 'absolute control' under Wiles' reign
item.description: A memo under new chief of staff Stephen Miller gives Cabinet secretaries messaging control, shifting from what sources say was Susie Wiles' grip.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: A memo describing the new White House hierarchy under chief of staff Stephen Miller circulated within the Trump administration this week, and details how Cabinet secretaries will now have more control over their own messaging.

This is a shift from what insiders say was administration-wide communications control implemented by former chief of staff Susie Wiles during the first nearly two years of President Donald Trump's second term.

"This will streamline the Cabinet, making it a more effective instrument for the President, whereas previously it was too constrained," a source familiar with the message told Fox News Digital.

The memo was sent by Miller's office after he took over the role on Monday. It was titled as a memo on administrative matters and personnel changes, the source said.

THE STONING OF STEPHEN MILLER, NOW RUNNING THE TRUMP WHITE HOUSE

"The White House position of Cabinet Secretary will be changed to the role of Director of Cabinet Relations, focused on providing support and reinforcement of President Trump's tremendous Cabinet Secretaries," details the memo, which Fox News Digital viewed.

"Each cabinet leader serves as the best leader and communicator for their individual Departments, and this new position will ensure our Cabinet is resourced and bolstered by the White House to deliver swift, critical, and lasting wins for the American people," the memo continues.

Another source who is familiar with day-to-day administration operations believes the memo signals a shift in communications policy, giving different agencies the ability to control their own messaging now that Miller has become chief of staff.

The source said that previously, they believe Wiles had a chokehold on nearly all the administration's communications, and that there were "a lot of prescriptive directives" from Wiles' camp.

"I mean, to me, it reflects well on Miller and his team and I think it's really smart to be making these moves quite clear, to be communicating clearly and effectively, you know?" the source said, speaking of the policy shake-up described in the memo.

The source added that the policy change is "unleashing the Cabinet to be the captains of their own ship."

"It's more [of] a recognition that you can't possibly effectively micromanage this wide of an organization and that sometimes it might be better to trust and invest in a support system that elevates the people who are closest to the issues," the source said.

TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY FACES FIRST MAJOR TEST AS WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING ROOM ENTERS NEW ERA

WHITE HOUSE THREATENS POLITICO WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' IF IT DOESN'T RETRACT SUSIE WILES REPORTING

A former Trump administration official had much more direct criticism of Wiles' management style.

"She wants complete authority," the source said.

"The control doesn't come from, 'hey, you have to do this.' The control comes from threat of duress. Like, 'if you don't do this, I'm going to destroy you in the media,'" they continued. "The thing is, she has been very clear. 'I can't control [Trump]. I can control everything else.'"

The source accused Wiles of approaching Cabinet secretaries and warning them that if they said anything off script in the media, that midterm GOP election losses would be blamed on them.

TRUMP CLOSING IN ON NEW PRESS SECRETARY AS ADMINISTRATION OFFICIALS PUSH FOR PICK WHO COULD BREAK THE MOLD

"It's absolute control," the source said.

The memo also highlights some hierarchical changes within the administration, saying the director of presidential scheduling and the Office of Presidential Scheduling will report directly to Chamberlain Harris, the deputy director of outer oval operations.

It also confirms previous reporting that Caleb Orr, formerly the assistant secretary of state for economic and business affairs, will become the chief of staff for policy.

"The White House will run a clear and regular policy process through the Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy and the National Security Advisor, with clearly defined responsibilities and assignments and no overlapping policy portfolios," the memo says.

Wiles did not return Fox News Digital's request for comment by time of publication.

item.title: Foreign spy ‘honeytraps’ targeting America’s tech elite spark alarm amid Nvidia CEO scandal
item.description: Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang raises urgent questions about honeytrap espionage targeting Silicon Valley.
item.content:encoded:
American tech executives are facing escalated and systematic campaigns by foreign intelligence services using a variety of spy tactics to get the upper hand, including "honeytraps," to infiltrate U.S. expert controls, supply chains and other intelligence, experts say.

The warning comes amid reports revealing NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese intelligence asset operating under corporate cover.

Foreign espionage operations targeting high-profile tech figures are not isolated incidents but reflect an ongoing, long-term threat designed to exploit business environments, former National Security Agency analyst and corporate cybersecurity expert Ira Winkler told Fox News Digital.

REBECCA GRANT: JENSEN HUANG OWES AMERICA AN APOLOGY, AND NVIDIA OWES INVESTORS ANSWERS

"In this case, this is what the honey trap was, where they used sex, apparently, as the way to establish a relationship that was apparently not necessarily coercion, but did maintain long-term access and play to the person's ego," Winkler said. "These types of cases have gone on over the last few decades and arguably since the days of Samson, if you want to get biblical on how long honey pots have been around."

Unlike traditional covert intelligence operations, foreign adversaries routinely target tech executives through legitimate business settings when their defenses are lowered, Winkler said.

"Tech events are prime targets, where people can go ahead and meet other people who might potentially have access," Winkler explained.

US ATTORNEY WARNS CHINESE ESPIONAGE IS 'EXTREMELY PERVASIVE,' SAYS BEIJING 'PLAYING THE LONG GAME'

He noted that chief executives rarely mingle on the street or in public venues. Instead, spies are deployed into professional settings in an effort to leverage opportunities to initiate contact.

In the case involving Nvidia, an artificial intelligence giant, Alice Huang was granted access through business interactions as an executive connected to the Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which federal investigators suspect functioned as a front to bypass export restrictions on AI hardware.

"This is where they had long-term access and clear cooperation in many cases, to go ahead to try to avoid export restrictions, to potentially get information," Winkler said. "Spies are trained on how to be social, how to meet people in social situations, wherever they might hang out and elevate the situations."

FBI OVERHAULS TECH BACKBONE TO COUNTER AI THREATS FROM FOREIGN ADVERSARIES, REDUCE RESPONSE TIMES, PATEL SAYS

The intersection of AI and foreign espionage has amplified scrutiny on Silicon Valley leadership. Intelligence officials have warned that top executives must treat routine networking as possible entry points for foreign state actors, Winkler said.

Security experts have stressed that human vulnerabilities remain the primary source through which U.S. adversaries attempt to undermine America's technological superiority.

HOW A FOREIGN GOVERNMENT HELPED ACCUSED SAUDI SPY'S FAMILY FLEE US AFTER OPENAI BUG SCANDAL

While popular portrayals of "honeytraps" focus on immediate extortion or coercion, modern corporate espionage generally focuses on long-term, sustained access, Winkler said.

Meaning, rather than a quick blackmail scheme, foreign intelligence services use personal relationships to build long-term influence to gather insights on executive decision-making.

"In this case, I doubt that there was that level of extortion," said Winkler. "But the fact that the woman was able to maintain a relationship with this person for years, apparently at this point in time, where the person was essentially acting on behalf of China, in some ways ... it does create questions."

item.title: Massive college football brawl ends with 23 players suspended, '90s TV app & ESPN's Laura Rutledge stays hot!
item.description: Second Hump Day of November Nightcaps breaks down 23 suspensions from the Arkansas-Pine Bluff and Grambling State brawl, plus CFP rankings drama.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Second Hump Day of November, folks. We're officially in the double-digit portion of the month.

Somehow, Thanksgiving is two weeks from tomorrow. How's that even possible? Feels like we were just grilling hamburgers for Labor Day, and now we're turkey shopping for the best deal with the big day just 15 days away.

Wild stuff.

More importantly, of course, is what today is: Veterans Day. I was at the Panera down the street this morning and saw three vets eating breakfast. One of them had on a hat similar to one my late grandfather used to wear religiously.

We struck up a conversation. I thanked him for his service. He thanked me for stopping by just to chat. There was nothing special about it. Nothing extraordinary. We had a couple laughs, made a couple jokes about the 157 different coffee options, and went on our ways.

SHOP VETERANS DAY DISCOUNTS ON BEDDING, CLOTHING, SHOES AND MORE, UP TO 60% OFF

It was simple, but important — to me, at least. He's the reason I was able to duck out of my house this morning and work from a coffee shop. We often forget about that on most days, which is fair given life is hectic and busy and stressful.

But I gotta say ... that one brief exchange made my day just a little better. I hope it did for him, too.

The little things in life really do go a long way.

Now, let's roll.

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where 23 college football players get slapped with a Saturday detention for beating the crap out of each other after last week's game.

You'll see.

What else? I've got a wild scoreboard graphic from last night's MACtion contest, our weekly 'Bash the CFP committee' fireside chat after last night's latest dump, and some '90s nostalgia to end the day.

Wait till you see this Roku channel the internet stumbled upon last night. Incredible.

OK, grab you a sundae for National Ice Cream Sundae Day, and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

I have no real take on ice cream sundaes. Everyone likes an ice cream sundae. Like french fries, its one of the few things we all tend to agree on.

AMERICA'S FAVORITE ICE CREAM FLAVOR REVEALED AS ONE CLASSIC TOPS EVERY STATE

My one hot take on ice cream? I contend that mint chocolate chip is the best flavor out there. I realize I'm in the minority on that, but I'll die on that hill. Don't knock it till you try it!

The Juice Bar on Nantucket has the best mint chocolate chip ice cream on the planet, by the way. You're welcome.

Can't hide money!

OK, let's get this class started with a wild postgame college football brawl last weekend between Arkansas-Pine Bluff and Grambling State that resulted in a whopping 23 (!!!) players getting suspended.

Probably a fair number, if I'm being honest:

"We’re extremely disappointed by the events that transpired during postgame of the Arkansas-Pine Bluff at Grambling State football game," SWAC Commissioner Dr. Charles McClelland said on Tuesday before issuing the suspension(s). "Acts of that nature have zero place in the Southwestern Athletic Conference and intercollegiate athletics. The Conference Office has and will continue to enforce a zero-tolerance policy for all acts deemed to be unsportsmanlike and contrary to the high standard of good sportsmanship we expect from all individuals associated with the athletics programs within our league."

The final tally? Nine players from Pine Bluff and 14 more from Grambling were suspended from that above brawl. In addition, each program was fined $25,000, which may sound like small potatoes, but these are HBCUs. That's a lot of money for those schools.

Remember, these are the schools that get paid upwards of a million dollars to get destroyed by P4 schools once or twice a year. There ain't a lot of wiggle room in the budget for a $25K fine.

Oh well. You live and learn!

Next? From SWACtion to MACtion, baby!

Goodness, college football is the best:

It there was ever a 90-second clip to perfectly display midweek MACtion, this is the one to use.

It was perfect. It's everything we love about college football. We're going to miss these moments in about two months, folks. Don't take them for granted. Don't waste a single second.

Now, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. How are we all feeling about the second batch of playoff rankings that were released last night?

Thoughts? Let me know! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

Two more on the way out, and they both involve a heavy dose of nostalgia. First? This has been making the rounds on Twitter today, and I have to admit, I am CAPTIVATED:

Just incredible. Do we have any Roku users here? Have y'all used this? Is it legit?

True story: About three years ago, I told my wife about this great idea I had for an app where it would literally just be an endless stream of commercials from the 1990s. That's it. Just different commercials from different channels on any given day from the '90s.

Feels like I missed a pretty big opportunity here, because someone took my idea and created something incredible. This thing would be on in my house 24/7 if I had Roku. You give me a chance to watch Catdog and an old Sears commercial from 1997, and I'm going to take it every single time. No-brainer.

Such a better time.

Finally, on the way out ... speaking of old things that were so much better:

"Black Friday used to mean fist fights at Walmart to get 60% off a TV. Now it’s a month-long event where you get 10% off a towel."

This is so true. Has anyone else noticed this? I was talking to my brother the other day about wanting one of those fancy frame TVs that are all the rage right now. The ones that basically look like a picture on the wall when you're not actually watching something.

Anyway, they're around $1,000, which is an absurd amount to pay for a TV in 2026. Naturally, I said I'd wait for Black Friday to see if I could find a steal.

"They're already all on Black Friday sales on Amazon right now," he said.

I looked. They are. Deals everywhere, and we're still weeks away from "Black Friday."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Makes me sad. Black Friday used to be a huge deal. Growing up, it was bigger than Thanksgiving for most folks.

Now? It's just another day. The deals have already started, and they're watered down because they run all month long.

Does anyone here still go to a department store on Black Friday? I'd love to hear what the scene is like in 2026.

OK, that's it for today. Good Hump Day, everyone. On that way out, here's ESPN's Laura Rutledge gearing up for another big week of FOOTBALL.

Take us home, Laura!

item.title: MMA fighters, including former UFC champ, get into wild melee at Abu Dhabi hotel lobby
item.description: Video captures Usman Nurmagomedov slapping Merab Dvalishvili in an Abu Dhabi hotel lobby, sparking a brawl that left the former UFC champ bloodied.
item.content:encoded:
A UFC rivalry appears to have been rekindled in Abu Dhabi this week ahead of an MMA event scheduled there this weekend.

Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili was jumped by MMA free agent Usman Nurmagomedov, the younger brother of Dvalishvili's former opponent, Umar Nurmagomedov, in a hotel lobby overseas.

Dvalishvili was recording an interview for Real American Freestyle when Usman Nurmagomedov and others approached behind him. Usman Nurmagomedov then slapped him across the face, and all hell broke loose.

At least six people were involved in the ruckus that left Dvalishvili bloodied.

"Was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend. Security was holding me - They kept kicking us when we were down like losers," Dvalishvili captioned an Instagram video of himself getting treatment.

"What a sneaky way, just two of us, me and my friend came here in Abu Dhabi, and Usman Nurmagomedov and his friends came like snakes from behind," Dvalishvili said in the post. "What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this? If you want to talk and fight, let's do it the real way. You guys came from f—ing - just because there's two of us, and you guys were prepared. What the f—?"

DANA WHITE TAKES QUESTIONS AT PODIUM DURING WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING WITH TRUMP

"We bleed, we fight, we war, but you guys are just sneaky guys," Dvalishvili continued. "You guys aren't real men. This shows your guys' character, shows you guys are not real men. What the f—, guys? If you want to fight, fight. Let's f—ing fight. We are fighters. I talk, I'm a real guy, I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys you was. All your friends, waiting for us in a sneaky way. Wow, bro. Wow. I knew what kind of guys you are. I just came here in Abu Dhabi and then Usman, Umar, and his friends came in a sneaky way and tried to beat us. So many guys."

Dvalishvili defeated Umar Nurmagomedov at UFC 311 in January 2025, where he defended the bantamweight title, which he eventually lost to Petr Yan the following December. He had a rematch against Yan on Oct. 24, 2026 for the title but lost. Both fights were by unanimous decision. Dvalishvili won the title at UFC 306 against Sean O'Malley and defended it against him at UFC 316 with President Donald Trump in attendance.

Dvalishvili's last fight against Yan was in Abu Dhabi, but he is staying there because he is due to fight Marlon Moraes at this Saturday's RAF event.

item.title: Texas Roadhouse goes beyond steak with new menu addition that has some fans questioning the move
item.description: Chicken Alfredo Pasta is being added to over 600 Texas Roadhouse locations as the chain is testing energizer drinks and mocktails across all three of its brands.
item.content:encoded:
Texas Roadhouse is expanding its Chicken Alfredo Pasta rollout and testing new nonalcoholic drinks across its three restaurant brands, according to a report.

The steakhouse chain added Chicken Alfredo Pasta to more than 600 locations in recent months and plans to bring it to the roughly 100 remaining locations by spring 2027, executives said during the company's third-quarter earnings call, Nation's Restaurant News reported.

Operators had asked for a new menu item, and early tests of the pasta proved popular with customers and staff, CEO Jerry Morgan said.

MAN SAYS TEXAS ROADHOUSE SERVED HIM $20 STEAK INSTEAD OF PRICIER FILET MULTIPLE TIMES

"It's a great choice for somebody who wants something a little bit different," Michael Bailen, vice president of investor relations for Texas Roadhouse, said.

Individual locations shared news of the penne pasta dish online, describing it as "creamy, cheesy and seriously delicious."

Some fans praised the dish, with one woman on Facebook saying it was "so good" and that she hoped it would remain on the menu permanently.

MEAT EXPERT SHARES THE MISTAKE MOST AMERICANS MAKE WHEN COOKING STEAK

Others, however, wondered what a pasta dish was doing on a steakhouse menu.

"Who goes to a steakhouse and orders chicken Alfredo?" one Reddit user said in a thread dedicated to Texas Roadhouse.

Bailen said the dish is "probably not going to be one of our top 10 mix entrée items that we offer, but it rounds out the menu."

Texas Roadhouse is also seeing continued demand for mocktails and dirty sodas, according to the report. The company is now testing "energizer" drinks at all three of its brands: Texas Roadhouse, Bubba's 33 and Jaggers.

The menu moves come as the company works to maintain momentum after sales growth slowed late in the third quarter, according to Nation's Restaurant News.

Executives attributed part of the slowdown to a viral social media hoax that falsely accused Texas Roadhouse and Logan's Roadhouse employees of planning to tamper with Black customers' food. The company investigated and concluded the claims were false.

Sales and traffic improved each week in October and continued to strengthen in early November, executives said.

Texas Roadhouse expects to open approximately 35 company-owned restaurants across its three brands in 2026, with another 35 planned for 2027.

"Maybe the recovery has taken a little bit longer than some would have expected, but our operators are out there busting their butts and they've doubled down on everything they're doing," Bailen said.
